modules.title: Official Codex plugin build surface
key_findings: Codex plugins use .codex-plugin/plugin.json as the required entry point.
Repo and personal marketplaces live at .agents/plugins/marketplace.json and point to local plugin folders with ./-prefixed source.path values.
The documented portable plugin surface is skills, optional .mcp.json, optional .app.json, and optional assets.
Manifest paths should stay relative to the plugin root and start with ./.
recommended_actions: Add .codex-plugin/plugin.json to each skill-bearing plugin folder.
Create a repo-scoped .agents/plugins/marketplace.json so the repo is installable in Codex without manual re-entry.
Use curated Codex-facing skill trees only when needed to avoid leaking host-specific Claude behavior into the Codex surface.

modules.title: Community validation and distribution practices

sources.title: Built an OSS CI gate for Codex plugins

key_findings: A community scanner workflow has emerged around codex-plugin-scanner lint/verify and a GitHub Action gate before wider distribution.
The awesome-codex-plugins registry uses a real repo marketplace and mirrored plugin folders, matching the official marketplace shape.
Registry maintainers treat validation evidence, plugin metadata quality, and packaging cleanliness as part of publish readiness.
recommended_actions: Keep the repo marketplace machine-readable and checked into source control.
Validate manifest JSON and marketplace JSON after generating them.
Document the local marketplace install path so users can test the repo as a curated Codex source.

modules.title: Dual manifest compatibility for Claude-first repositories

sources.title: Consider adding a .codex-plugin/plugin.json manifest for Codex discoverability

key_findings: A practical migration pattern is to keep the existing .claude-plugin manifest and add a .codex-plugin manifest alongside it.
Codex discoverability is tied directly to the presence of .codex-plugin/plugin.json, even for repositories that already ship Claude plugins.
Community feedback frames the Codex manifest as the low-risk compatibility layer rather than a full repository rewrite.
recommended_actions: Preserve the Claude plugin manifests untouched and add parallel Codex manifests.
Reuse stable plugin names and versions across both manifests to avoid identity drift.
Document which repository surfaces remain host-specific after the Codex port.

modules.title: Thin Codex wrapper patterns around skills and MCP
key_findings: A common Codex plugin pattern is a thin wrapper: keep runtime wiring small, put guidance in skills, and keep plugin metadata explicit.
The example plugin keeps its MCP wiring in .mcp.json and uses the manifest to describe install behavior and discovery metadata.
Community examples emphasize staying close to upstream tools instead of forking or re-implementing them inside the plugin.
recommended_actions: Port the existing skill-bearing plugins first instead of trying to re-create every Claude-specific surface in Codex.
Leave unsupported host-specific behavior out of the Codex manifests unless the repo actually bundles the needed Codex surface.
Use README notes to explain the thin-wrapper boundary and any host-specific limitations.

modules.title: Repository application plan for claude-swift-toolkit
key_findings: The truthful Codex surface now includes the four lifecycle plugins: apple-app-architect, apple-design-system, apple-app-builder, and apple-app-quality.

apple-app-builder and apple-app-quality now bundle plugin-local .mcp.json files that launch the official Xcode MCP bridge via xcrun mcpbridge, making their Xcode-backed build and test workflows explicit in the Codex package.
hookify currently depends on Claude-specific commands, agents, and hooks and does not expose a Codex-ready skill, app, or MCP surface.

The least-risk transformation remains a dual-host rollout: keep the Claude-first structure intact, use Codex-facing wrapper skill trees only where host behavior diverges, and document hookify as Claude-only.
recommended_actions: Keep the repo marketplace aligned with the full Codex-supported lifecycle plugin set.
Update the root README with Codex installation steps, the current support matrix, and the official Xcode MCP bridge prerequisite notes for builder and quality workflows.
Record the research synthesis in-repo so future plugin changes can reuse the migration rationale.
